data.title: Anthropic Outspends OpenAI On Federal Lobbying
data.description:
Anthropic nearly tripled its federal lobbying spend to $3.53 million, outpacing OpenAI by more than $1 million in the first half of 2026. According to BeInCrypto, federal disclosures show Anthropic added the Treasury Department to its list of lobbied agencies for the first time this quarter, while OpenAI nearly doubled spending to a record $2.22 million.

Issue One counted $41 million in combined spending from January to June across 11 major technology, social media and AI companies and their trade associations, with Kalshi also spending $990,000 on lobbying in the first half of 2026.

data.title: Baker Hughes Says Iran Conflict Impact on Some Projects and Supply Chains to Be Offset
data.description: According to Jin10, Baker Hughes said the impact of the Iran conflict on some projects and supply chains is expected to be offset by strong performance in other regions.

data.title: STOCKS | Nasdaq 100 Turns Lower After Giving Back Some Gains
data.description: U.S. stocks gave back part of their gains, and the Nasdaq 100 Index briefly turned lower. According to Jin10, the Nasdaq 100 Index once fell into negative territory.

data.title: Crypto Liquidations Hit $313 Million in 24 Hours
data.description:
Crypto liquidations totaled $313 million across the market in the past 24 hours, according to Coinglass. According to ChainCatcher, long positions accounted for $83.98 million of the total, while short positions made up $229 million.

Bitcoin liquidations included $7.8 million in long positions and $45.11 million in short positions. Ethereum liquidations included $21.08 million in long positions and $113 million in short positions.

Over the same 24-hour period, 91,007 traders were liquidated worldwide. The largest single liquidation was an Aster ETHUSDT position worth $8.72 million.

data.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Extend Decline
data.description: U.S. natural gas futures fell, influenced by several factors, including reduced risk that August heat will boost power-sector demand and lower oil and European natural gas prices after the United States paused military strikes on Iran. According to Jin10, EBW Analytics analyst Eli Rubin said weak liquefied natural gas feedgas demand and rising production have worsened the soft outlook, while Texas heat may offer short-term support and falling temperatures along the Gulf Coast and in the Southeast may limit upside price risk.

data.title: STOCKS | UBS Group Cuts Microsoft Price Target to $480 From $510
data.description: UBS Group lowered its price target on Microsoft (MSFT.O) to $480 from $510. According to Jin10, the bank made the adjustment.

data.title: STOCKS | Robeco's $18 Billion Stock Picker Bets on Argentina After Hiatus
data.description:
Robeco’s $18 billion emerging-market stock picker has returned to Argentine equities after nearly a decade away, according to Bloomberg.

The move marks a renewed bet on Argentina by one of Europe’s biggest emerging-market investors.

data.title: Governance Gap Leaves Johannesburg $12 Billion Behind Cape Town
data.description:
Cape Town has opened a gap of at least $12 billion in commercial property values over Johannesburg as the two South African cities diverge in governance, according to Bloomberg.

The gap highlights Cape Town’s lead in commercial real estate relative to Johannesburg, South Africa’s largest city.

data.title: STOCKS | Nvidia Credit Risk Jumps on $750 Billion AI Deal Talk
data.description:
The cost of insuring Nvidia Corp.’s debt against default surged by the most on record on Monday after reports it is in talks on more than $750 billion of artificial intelligence infrastructure deals, according to Bloomberg.

The move fueled concern that the chipmaker could be taking on additional obligations as it expands its AI push.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Treasury Yields Track Oil Lower as Fed, Supply Stay in Focus
data.description:
US Treasuries edged higher as oil prices softened after the US paused its nearly two-week campaign of strikes against Iran, while traders priced in a roughly one-in-three chance of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike on Wednesday, according to Bloomberg.

Supply concerns also remained in focus for the bond market.

data.title: Swiss National Bank Sees Zero Rate Through End of 2027
data.description:
The Swiss National Bank expects to keep its key interest rate at zero until the end of 2027 before probably beginning to raise it, according to people familiar with the central bank’s thinking, Bloomberg reported.

The outlook suggests Swiss policymakers see no need to tighten monetary policy for more than two years.

data.title: Chile Returns to International Bond Markets After Debt Limit Increase
data.description: Chile is returning to international debt markets for the second time in 2026, a few weeks after Congress raised the limit on sovereign bond sales this year, according to Bloomberg. The move comes after lawmakers increased the ceiling for sovereign bond issuance, allowing the government to tap external funding again.

data.title: Nvidia to Make Large-Scale Investment in Safe Superintelligence, The Wall Street Journal Says
data.description: According to Jin10, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia will make a large-scale investment in Safe Superintelligence, founded by OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever.

data.title: Crypto Is Rewriting How Wall Street Traders Spend Their Weekends
data.description: Around-the-clock crypto markets are forcing Wall Street to rethink one of its oldest assumptions: that weekends are for waiting. The nonstop trading environment is changing how market participants manage risk and respond to price moves, according to CoinDesk, even as traditional markets still close for the weekend.

data.title: Goldman Bullish On Won, Taiwan Dollar, Ringgit On AI Spending Boom
data.description:
Goldman Sachs is bullish on the South Korean won, Taiwan dollar and Malaysian ringgit, saying Asia’s AI investment boom is reshaping foreign exchange markets. The bank expects those currencies to outperform energy importers such as the Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah, according to BeInCrypto, as chip exporters benefit and oil buyers lag.

Goldman sees South Korea’s current account surplus nearly doubling to roughly $300 billion this year, while Taiwan’s surplus could reach 25% of GDP. It also cites resilient AI-led growth, strong exports and foreign direct investment as support for the ringgit.

data.title: Yemeni Houthis Say They Targeted Saudi Crude Transport Infrastructure With Drones
data.description: A statement said the Yemeni Houthis used drones to target Saudi crude transport infrastructure. According to Jin10, the statement was released by the Yemeni Houthis.

data.title: Saudi Aramco Jazan Refinery Tank Appears on Fire After Houthi Attack
data.description:
A tank at Saudi Aramco's Jazan oil refinery appeared to be on fire in satellite images taken after Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on the plant over the weekend, according to Bloomberg.

The satellite imagery showed the blaze after the reported strike, but the source did not provide additional damage details.

data.title: Amazon Leo Seeks FCC Approval for Up to 5,105 New Satellites
data.description: According to Jin10, Amazon Leo has filed an application with the FCC to deploy up to 5,105 new satellites.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Naver Expects 200 MW AI Factory to Use Nvidia Vera Rubin and Blackwell Platforms
data.description: Naver said its 200-megawatt AI factory is expected to use advanced AI infrastructure, including Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Blackwell platforms. According to Jin10, the company made the statement in the source article.
